pillar_reactions.evidence: Arrived pre-sold on it from Instagram and tied it to his own diagnosis unprompted: 'the workouts he was doing, it just comes across a lot more dynamic, more about motion, more about flexibility, rather than just kind of sitting behind, underneath a bench and lifting weights.' After the presentation: 'Yeah, totally. It's all kind of ticking the box is what I was looking for.' He also contrasted it favourably with a friend who trains legs once every three weeks purely for upper-body size — 'for me, there's a lot of other things that are at play here. It's not just about the kind of, oh, I want to look good.'

Asked directly whether he had questions and said no — 'I think it's, it's a new approach that I have to, to kind of lean into.' He volunteered his own intermittent fasting history and, importantly, conceded the diagnosis: 'I under eat a lot' and 'I know nutrition is a major part of how my body is going to change, and I admit that yes, I'm not the most strict, but that's why I can't follow these programs where it's so regimental, and I think that's why when I saw, when I hear about it like this, it changes the picture.' Note roughly eighty seconds of this pillar is missing from the recording due to a connection dropout.

Named all three pillars back and endorsed them: 'it kind of was just hearing all the right words. And that's exactly what I need from all three standpoints, from changing the type of workout to helping with balance, that nutrition, and having that accountability, I think are the three great pillars. And it's exactly what I need.' He also tied it to his own deeper why — proving he can be disciplined — and to a life event: 'I'm also moving to the US in the next month. So it's kind of like all ties in and fitting in with this new, new kind of fresh start.'

anchors.raw: my brother has been on the past year, he's been on an extremely regimental program with a PT, and he's been working out and he's kind of given me some inspiration for the workouts I do now, and to see his body change in the past year... I've seen significant results because he takes those weekly photos and sometimes I'm taking them for him. ... And we have very similar physiques in terms of the skin. So the proof of concept is already there.
anchors.note: The most powerful anchor on the call and it works entirely for the offer. Someone with his genetics and his body type paid for structured coaching for a year and it worked, which pre-destroys the 'it's just my genes' escape route. He raised it himself while being pressed on whether the status quo was acceptable, and it is the reason a $6,000 price landed without resistance.

anchors.raw: sometimes you look at these PTs and I'm like, I don't want to pay stupid amounts of money for results that, you know, are not going to really be seen, but it's because sometimes I don't believe in the, the idea of what they're showing me. Like I've had PTs come over and give me a training session and I'm like, okay, you're not giving me anything that's like significantly different to what I'm doing now.
anchors.note: Reads as a price objection but is the opposite. He has already rejected cheaper trainers on differentiation, not cost, and explicitly separates Primal from them: 'that's why I think this one was different for me, because I saw it myself, and then I reached out, and I made that kind of effort myself rather than someone reaching out to me.' Price is a quality signal to him.

anchors.raw: you see things on Instagram all the time, right? And it's like paying without trying.
anchors.note: The one anchor that cost money. A general expectation that a digital fitness purchase should be trialled first, combined with wanting to meet the coach, is what triggered the rep to drop from $6,000 collected today to $1,200 collected tomorrow. Same anchor, same improvised answer, as on the 06/24 Jean-Philippe Rifaat call.

unmet_demand.want: To meet Trevor before paying, so he knows who he will be training with before committing a significant sum
unmet_demand.why_unmet: The process places payment strictly first and there is no pre-purchase contact with the coach: 'So the process is that it's always after after payment.' The scarcity argument given — 'our calendars are packed' — is an operational reason, not a product one. The same request and the same refusal appear in the 06/29 team meeting for a different prospect, so this is recurring demand, not a one-off.

unmet_demand.want: A way to try the coaching before committing to six months
unmet_demand.why_unmet: No trial exists in the offer. One was improvised at $1,200 with a $4,800 top-up. It converted him, which is the point worth escalating: this is the second call in the batch where the same invented trial resolved the same objection, and it is being priced live rather than designed.

unmet_demand.want: To pay from GBP holdings without same-day settlement pressure
unmet_demand.why_unmet: Checkout expects immediate payment in dollars and the prospect holds most of his money in pounds while sitting in the US — 'my money is in both places, because it's in dollars, right? ... Mainly my money's in pounds, so I have to, let me sort something out.' Whether this is a real barrier or simply an unworked objection is genuinely unclear; it cost this deal a same-call collection and is worth checking against other non-US prospects.
